explanation: The theorem says that (ℓ − 1) times the cuspidal divisor on the library's modular curve is principal. Its witness is the library's own modular unit `ubar ℓ …`. Everything in the statement and proof comes from the library: `cuspidalDivisor`, `Divisor.IsPrincipal`, `ubar`, `modularUnitSeries` and `smul_cuspidalDivisor_apply`. Mathlib has no modular curves over number fields, no cuspidal divisors and no modular units in this sense, so no Mathlib declaration can state this result or have it as a special case. All of the mathematical content is in the library's own definitions and lemmas. I did not run a separate grep of Mathlib for this.
